blind_spots.blind_spot: A commercial cloud FDM/FOQA backend holding SOF mission flight data
blind_spots.operator_reality: AFSOC and AMC flight-data recordings are not airline FOQA. Routes, tanker tracks, LZ approaches and aircraft performance in aggregate are mission-revealing; that is CUI at best and classified in composite. Standing that up on government networks means an IL5 boundary, STIGs, a POA&M and a named ISSO — and the ten roles currently open at Beacon contain no security or compliance engineer at all. The accreditation clock, not the software, is what will consume the Phase 3 period of performance.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The same platform serves airlines and charter operators, where cloud FDM is the norm and the only regulator is the FAA — so the architecture was validated by a commercial customer set before SOCOM ever saw it.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Web and cloud-based aviation intelligence platform. Gives actionable insights for Aircraft Operator FDM/FOQA and FDM-B (enhanced flight data monitoring data).

blind_spots.blind_spot: An iOS/EFB delivery path that assumes a device the vendor can update
blind_spots.operator_reality: Half the open engineering roles are iOS/mobile, including one explicitly for the Electronic Flight Bag. On a military airframe the EFB tablet is GFE running a locked baseline under unit MDM, with a Class 2 EFB mounting and airworthiness release behind it. There is no App Store channel, no TestFlight, and a software update is a configuration-control action measured in months. A product whose iteration loop assumes mobile-app release cadence stalls the moment it meets the aircraft.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their comparative advantage is stated as self-driving-car software speed applied to aviation, so fast iteration is the identity of the company rather than a variable to be traded away.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Software Engineer, iOS/Mobile - Electronic Flight Bag (EFB)

blind_spots.blind_spot: Debrief and fleet-monitoring value that only materializes when the aircraft can offload data
blind_spots.operator_reality: 'Flight debrief & playback', 'Live flight support' and 'Fleet Monitoring' all presume a data path off the airframe. SOF aviation flies emissions-controlled, often with no permissible RF transmission for the whole sortie, and lands at bare bases with no accredited ground network to sideload to. The offload becomes a hand-carried encrypted drive and a two-person custody procedure — which is exactly the frame-rate-decoupling problem in a different costume: the architecture assumed a link the environment denies, and the fix is designing for deferred, chunked, integrity-checked offload rather than 'live'.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The commercial fleets they also serve land at airports with wifi and ground handling; nothing in the airline case surfaces EMCON as a design input.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Assistant and platform to aid in flight safety and operational efficiency ... Flight debrief & playback ... Live flight support ... Fleet Monitoring

opener_hook: The $49.5M Phase 3 OTA you signed with USSOCOM on April 15 is a production vehicle, and all ten roles open on your careers page are software — frontend, cloud, iOS, LLM — with no ISSO, flight test, or field integration among them.
what_they_do: Builds an AI copilot for professional flight decks — an edge-compute EFB assistant plus a cloud flight-data platform — for airlines and, increasingly, SOCOM and Air Mobility Command aircrew.
